# Lupine Science

> Lupine Science measures where machine-learned models of atoms go wrong, against published references and pass/fail gates set in advance, and publishes every verdict, failures included. It is an early-stage, founder-led research company. We independently measure the errors of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), test corrections against preregistered gates, record any amendment made after results are seen, and publish the verdict: pass, fail or abstain. Correction is a research question here, not a product: it has held only in narrow, stated cases. Nothing we have published is peer-reviewed yet.

Updated: 2026-11-12

## Company facts

- Mission: Make AI predictions of new materials checkable before a lab commits to them.
- Stage: Early stage, founder-led
- Founder: Alex Welcing
- Contact: Research partners, model builders, press and investors: alex@lupinesci.com
- Phone: 940-400-0727 (https://lupine.science/contact/)
- Next public appearance: TMS2027 Annual Meeting & Exhibition, Orlando, 14–18 March 2027; poster presentation: https://lupine.science/articles/tms-2027-measuring-what-we-can-trust/
- Licences: You can reuse our code (MIT) and our first-party text and data (CC BY 4.0) with attribution and no share-alike obligations.

## Publication status

No Lupine paper has been peer-reviewed or accepted yet. Articles on
lupine.science are published on this site only, and each carries its own
status label.

A poster abstract was accepted for TMS2027 (Orlando, 14–18 March 2027). It is a conference presentation, not a paper. The accepted abstract described a universal error 'hyper-ribbon'; our record no longer supports that, and the proceedings manuscript replaces it with narrower measurement claims.

Lean 4 checks the arithmetic and stated inequalities behind published numbers; it does not check the physics, the reference data or the pipeline.
